doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Biagini, Duke and the Shaw band
title: Berigan, Louis Armstrong and Teagarden as influences
summary: Best names Bunny Berigan as idol and Louis and Jack Teagarden as top influences.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Right, okay. I wanted to ask you something, you were taking about listening to Louis Armstrong, and that you considered those records to be older stuff, that you had to go back and listen to. But this was late 1930s you were talking about, right? And Louis had recorded those records only about ten years before that. Is that right? So it really wasn’t that big a space between the time when you had to go back and listen to him, it was only ten years, is that right? So really it kind of wasn’t that old.

Well what kind of burned those guys up a little bit, the ones that were talking about the old Louis, my favorite trumpet player by that time was Bunny Berigan. He was my idol. And when I heard Bunny I just said well that’s it. But Bunny’s favorite was Louis. And that’s what they told me, they said, “Where do you think he learned to play from?” So you learn, a little bit at a time.
Well you were getting your Louis through Bunny, then, right?

Well I liked Beiderbecke too. But Louis always, when I listened to his old records, it’s amazing. And also Jack Teagarden. Probably of all the musicians that I ever listened to of course Louis and Jack Teagarden would probably be the top of my list, those guys.
